meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Relational Russian adjective in '-ский' meaning 'Russian', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Russian. Orthodox. Never been in prison.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('French').

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('Japanese').

examples.trans: Wow, a tape recorder! A Japanese one!

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('they') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'зывать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'назвать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to designate') (to assign a title) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Call me simply Lev from now on.

examples.text: А вы называйте меня просто Вика.
examples.trans: And you call me simply Vika.

examples.text: Они называют себя лучшим рестораном города.
examples.trans: They call themselves the best restaurant in town.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

the plural is used only in this sense
the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'pizza', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: All right, call your pizza place.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'matter', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

Secondary conversational sense ('case (in court)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ты точно понял, как нужно правильно нарезать этот стейк?
